title: H486 — Dynamic Multi-Strategy Capital Allocation via Online Portfolio Selection (universal-portfolios)
rationale: Tonight's wiki expansion (paper-trading/dynamic-strategy-allocation.md) identified that every existing allocation framework in the wiki (performance-attribution.md's Brinson sleeve attribution, strategy-blending-correlation.md's IC-weighted blending) uses STATIC target weights across the 7 production sleeves (H026/H041a/H045/H174 PEAD/XLK-SMH-IGV IBS). The pip-installable `universal-portfolios` package (Marigold, 858 stars, actively maintained) implements 20+ Online Portfolio Selection algorithms (OLMAR, CRP, Anticor, PAMR, CORN, RMR, Universal Portfolio) that are asset-agnostic and can be run against a DataFrame of sleeve NAV series instead of individual asset prices. This is a well-scoped, low-cost backtest (library already installable, sleeve NAV history already exists in strategy_accounts.json) to test whether dynamic reweighting beats the current static blend (OOS Sharpe 4.158, MaxDD -3.60%) enough to justify the added operational complexity of a non-static rebalance schedule.
content:
Script scaffold for H486 dynamic multi-strategy allocation.

Phase 1 (data prep): Build nav_df -- a DataFrame indexed by date, columns = strategy sleeve names (H026, H041a, H045, H174_PEAD, XLK_IBS, SMH_IBS, IGV_IBS), values = cumulative NAV per sleeve. Source: strategy_accounts.json equity history (paper trading) is too short for a real backtest -- use each sleeve's own run_hNNN.py backtest equity curve output (already computed OOS 2018+/2021+ per sleeve) resampled to a common daily/monthly frequency instead.

Phase 2 (baseline replication): Reproduce the current static target-weight blend (H026 27% / H041a 22% / H045 21% / XLK IBS 20% / SMH IBS 8% / IGV IBS 2%, no H174 weight documented -- confirm production weights before running) as the OOS Sharpe 4.158 / MaxDD -3.60% baseline. This step is a sanity check -- must match the known number before proceeding.

Phase 3 (OPS backtest): pip install universal-portfolios. Run OLMAR(window=5, eps=10) and CRP() from `universal.algos` against nav_df. Compare resulting OOS Sharpe/MaxDD/turnover vs. the static baseline.

Gate: dynamically-reweighted blend OOS Sharpe > 4.158 AND MaxDD not worse than -5.00% (baseline -3.60% + 1.4pp tolerance, matching the standard 5pp-improvement-or-no-regression gate pattern used elsewhere in the hypothesis log).

Known risk: OPS algorithms assume free daily rebalancing into any 'asset' -- our sleeves have mismatched native cadences (H026/H041a/H045 monthly, IBS sleeves near-daily, PEAD event-driven). If Phase 3 passes the gate on paper, a follow-up step must confirm the *achievable* rebalance frequency (e.g. weekly target-weight recompute feeding into each sleeve's existing monthly/daily scripts) doesn't erode the improvement via added turnover/transaction costs -- see transaction-costs.md gate methodology.
